newsitem.title: USA: Group not backing Wallace rival slate.
newsitem.headline: Group not backing Wallace rival slate.

text.p: Wyser-Pratte & Co Inc said on Wednesday that Institutional Shareholder Services Inc is not supporting its nominees to Wallace Computer Services Inc's board, but the group is backing a Wyser-Pratte proposal to change a by-law amendment.

The advisory firm that makes recommendations to institutional shareholders has recommended that its clients vote for a tender offer by-law amendment at Wallace Computer Services Inc's annual meeting on November 6.
Institutional Shareholder Services did not support Wyser-Pratte's business combination statute proposal, Wyser-Pratte said.

Wyser-Pratte, which holds about 2.3 percent of Wallace, said the tender offer by-law amendment requires shareholder approval if Wallace's board were to oppose a qualified, all-cash tender offer for more than 90 days following the beginning of the offer.

The report by Institutional Shareholder Services also criticized Goldman Sachs's valuation calculation on Wallace Computer, which was used as a basis to reject Moore Corp Ltd's acquisition offer, Wyser-Pratte said.

Goldman based its price to earnings multiple on the price of Wallace's shares the day before the bid, Wyser-Pratte said. However, the Institutional Shareholder Services report claims that Wallace's share value was inflated by rumors of the bid on that date, Wyser-Pratte said.
Goldman Sachs was not immediately available for comment.
Moore Corp withdrew the bid in August after a lengthy takeover battle.
A Goldman Sachs spokesman later said about Wyser-Pratte: "This is yet another effort by Mr. Wyser-Pratte to distort a record that was vindicated by the courts."
